title: Run dual BLE connection test on Pi with iPhone
notes:
RESULT: PM5 supports only ONE simultaneous BLE connection.

Test performed 2026-08-08 on Pi (edge-04, 192.168.12.32) against a real PM5
(serial 530426599) with the Concept2 iPhone app connected. Confirmed via
4 independent test runs (3 manual + 1 fully automated):

1. Scan-based: PM5 stops advertising entirely once the iPhone holds a
   connection (invisible to BleakScanner.discover, confirmed both directions
   -- appears when iPhone disconnects, vanishes again when it reconnects).
2. Bonded-device connect: even after pairing/bonding the Pi to the PM5
   (giving BlueZ a persistent, non-ephemeral device object independent of
   advertising), `bluetoothctl connect <addr>` fails after ~40s with
   `org.bluez.Error.Failed le-connection-abort-by-local` while the iPhone
   is connected.
3. Bracket-checked: confirmed via scan immediately before AND after the
   connect attempt that the PM5 remained non-advertising throughout --
   i.e. the iPhone's connection held the entire time, ruling out a false
   result from a mid-test drop. (One earlier run DID produce a false PASS
   this way, caused by the iPhone's screen-lock silently dropping its
   connection mid-test -- this is why the bracket check exists.)
4. The existing (iPhone) connection is unaffected/stable throughout a
   failed second connection attempt -- failure mode is "2nd client locked
   out", not "both destabilized".

Test script: docs/planning/legacy/examples/test_dual_ble.py (commit 680a723)
-- restored from unmerged branch origin/docs/detailed-planning (4f5ae1e) and
hardened with the bonded-fallback + bracket-check logic above so it's fully
re-runnable without manual bluetoothctl choreography.

Side finding: PM5 also exposes the standard BLE Fitness Machine Service
(0x1826, Rower Data characteristic 0x2AD1) alongside the Concept2 proprietary
service -- worth considering as an alternative interface.

ARCHITECTURE IMPLICATION (feeds c2m-ooz.2 / ADR-001): concept2mqtt must be
the sole BLE gateway to the PM5. Other consumers (e.g. a coaching app) must
go through concept2mqtt's MQTT relay rather than connecting directly.
Considered-and-deferred alternative: Pi holds the sole PM5 connection while
also emulating a PM5 as a BLE peripheral (dual central+peripheral role) for
other devices to connect to -- technically plausible, real added complexity,
untested whether this Pi's BLE chip supports concurrent dual-role operation.
close_reason: PM5 confirmed to support only 1 simultaneous BLE connection (4 independent test runs, incl. bonded-device connect + bracket-checked to rule out false positives). Test script committed at 680a723. Unblocks c2m-ooz.2 (ADR-001).

title: Add Rust crate coverage to CI pipeline
description:
## Problem

The CI `ci:test:unit` task only measures Python coverage via pytest-cov. The Rust
`csafe-codec` crate has its own test suite (passes in "Rust Checks" job) but coverage
is not collected or reported. The Python coverage gate (`--fail-under=80`) fails with
0% because the Python tests exercise Rust FFI bindings, not Python source.

## Scope

1. Add a Taskfile task (e.g. `ci:test:rust-coverage`) that runs `cargo llvm-cov` for
   `csafe-codec` and outputs lcov/xml coverage.
2. Update the CI workflow to collect Rust coverage and upload it to Codecov alongside
   Python coverage (separate flags/components).
3. Fix the Python `ci:test:unit` task so it does not fail when there is no Python
   source to measure (either skip the gate or adjust `--fail-under` dynamically).
4. Add `CODECOV_TOKEN` repo secret (manual step, documented).

## Acceptance criteria

- `task ci:test:unit` passes when no Python source is covered.
- Rust test coverage is visible in Codecov under a separate flag.
- CI green on both Python-only and Rust-only PRs.
close_reason: Implemented cargo-llvm-cov coverage pipeline with Codecov flags

title: PM5 relay: auto-reconnect the central PM5 link and resume advertising
description:
R-RELAY-2 and R-OPS-3 from the 2026-09-05 hardware validation.

The relay has no disconnect handling at all: run() awaits asyncio.Event().wait() forever and the BleakClient is created without a disconnected_callback. When the PM5 dropped at 21:53 on 2026-09-05 the relay sat idle with frozen stats for 4 hours and never recovered (findings section 8).

R-RELAY-2: on a central-side drop, reconnect to the PM5 with backoff WITHOUT tearing down the peripheral, and resume relaying (re-subscribe the streaming characteristics on the new link). The emulated peripheral and the consumer's connection must survive.

R-OPS-3: on consumer disconnect, make sure the peripheral is advertising again promptly so the app can re-discover it without manual intervention. Whether BlueZ already resumes a registered advertisement on disconnect is NOT established -- the section 8 observation was confounded by the phone auto-reconnecting a bond, which c2m-ooz.3.2 removes. Log consumer connect/disconnect so the next run settles it either way.

Blocks a trustworthy Step D: that is a >=20 min continuous piece plus app background/reconnect cycles, and a PM5 blip currently kills the run silently.
notes: Implemented and landed 2026-09-06 (commits 57bf102, aad17bf). R-RELAY-2: disconnected_callback wakes a supervisor loop that reconnects with exponential backoff (2s-60s) and calls rebind_central() to resubscribe on the new link; peripheral and consumer connection are left untouched. R-OPS-3: polls the peripheral adapter's Device1.Connected to log consumer connect/disconnect and re-registers the advertisement on the disconnect edge (whether BlueZ already did this on its own was never established — now settled either way by the new log). Also picked up the SIGINT/SIGTERM defect in the same area (aad17bf): the relay relied on KeyboardInterrupt, which never fires under setsid with no controlling terminal, so the documented pkill -INT stop procedure silently left the PM5 connected; fixed with explicit asyncio signal handlers. Not hardware-verified yet -- rolled into c2m-ooz.3.3's end-to-end session (reconnect-survives-a-drop and resume-advertising-after-disconnect are both on that checklist).
close_reason: Implemented and landed (57bf102, aad17bf); hardware re-verification rolled into c2m-ooz.3.3

title: PM5 relay: consumer connection unstable across relay restarts (bond / GATT-cache)
description:
Hardware validation 2026-09-05. After ANY relay restart, the iPhone app finds the advertised device and shows the pairing prompt, the user accepts, and then the connection never completes - no GATT discovery, no consumer reads reach the relay. Observed repeatedly (22:46, 23:09).

The only reliable recovery seen:
  stop relay
  rm -rf /var/lib/bluetooth/<hci1-addr>/<phone-addr> and .../cache/*
  systemctl restart bluetooth   (this also kills the relay's BlueZ registrations - restart relay after)
  restart relay
  'Forget This Device' on the iPhone
  connect fresh
Both successful rows this session (22:31, 22:59) came immediately after such a wipe.

Likely cause: bluez-peripheral assigns GATT attribute handles dynamically, so the attribute layout shifts every restart; a bonded iOS client keeps its cached layout and there is no working Service Changed path, so discovery breaks on reconnect.

Candidate fixes: stable/fixed GATT handles across restarts; OR non-bondable 'just works' peripheral (no stored keys) - need to confirm whether the real PM5 bonds or uses just-works; OR a Service Changed indication iOS honours; OR persist the peripheral identity+GATT db.

Blocks Step C re-verification and Step D. See docs/planning/log/pm5-ble-relay-hardware-validation-findings.md section 8 (R-PAIR-1, R-GATT-STABLE-1).
notes:
2026-09-06 (dev container, Pi unreachable -- NOT hardware-verified).

Three defects found in relay_pm5.py, all fixed in commit 1fe4725:
1. NoIoAgent was registered and the adapter left bondable -> iOS bonded, then trusted its cached attribute layout instead of re-discovering. This is the trap.
2. stop() called Advertisement.release(), which DOES NOT EXIST in bluez-peripheral; contextlib.suppress swallowed the AttributeError. The advertisement was never unregistered, even on a clean SIGINT.
3. stop() called the ASYNC ServiceCollection.unregister() without awaiting it -> GATT application never unregistered either.

So findings section 8's 'ungraceful kill leaves a stale advertising registration' was really 'EVERY shutdown leaves one'.

Fixes: no pairing agent; Pairable=false; forget devices already bonded to the peripheral adapter at startup; power-cycle the adapter on startup (scripted hciconfig down/up); unregister both advert (via LEAdvertisingManager1) and GATT application on shutdown, logging failures instead of suppressing them.

Expected next run: no pairing prompt, no bond, restart needs no wipe on either side. If the app STILL fails to connect after a restart, R-GATT-STABLE-1 (fixed handles / Service Changed indication) is the remaining cause -- reopen against that.

Validation doc gained a 2.1 'Restarting the relay' section. See findings doc section 14.1.
2026-09-06 HARDWARE VERIFIED on edge-04 (new IP 192.168.12.114), kernel 6.18.42-v8+, hci1 CSR8510.

Ran BluezPeripheralServer start/stop standalone (no PM5 needed):
- Pairable=False, Discoverable=False, Powered=True on every start -> the non-bondable fix works and needs no extra polkit privilege.
- ActiveInstances=1 while running, and 0 after stop() -> the advertisement is genuinely unregistered now. Under the old code Advertisement.release() raised AttributeError into contextlib.suppress, so this stayed 1 forever. Defects 2+3 proven fixed.
- Three consecutive start/stop cycles, 0 failures, no warnings from stop(). The 'Failed to register advertisement' stale-registration failure on restart is gone.

STILL UNVERIFIED (needs the iPhone): that the app connects with no pairing prompt and reconnects after a relay restart without a both-sides wipe. That is the end-to-end claim -> c2m-ooz.3.3.
close_reason: Three defects found and fixed (1fe4725); peripheral-side hardware-verified 2026-09-06 (findings 14.3: non-bondable, ActiveInstances 1->0 across stop(), 3 clean restart cycles). End-to-end iPhone re-verification (no pairing prompt, reconnect without a wipe) rolled into c2m-ooz.3.3

title: PM5 relay adds ~1s telemetry latency (direct connection is ~0.15s)
description:
Hardware validation 2026-09-05. Display->app lag measured ~1.2s through the relay (up to ~3s when perturbed), vs ~0.15s when the iPhone connects DIRECTLY to the PM5. So the ~1s is added by the relay, not the PM5's cadence.

Leading hypotheses:
1. The app's ce060034 (sample-rate) write does not take effect through the relay. Direct, the app writes ce060034 and the PM5 speeds up. Through the relay the same write is logged as 8 bytes and forwarded, but the PM5 keeps streaming General Status at ~1Hz on the relay's central link -> the relayed write is rejected/mangled (length? write vs write-without-response? timing?). This alone explains ~1s.
2. Forward-path overhead: bleak PropertiesChanged in -> asyncio -> bluez-peripheral notify D-Bus call out -> BlueZ -> 30ms legacy link. Note: forcing a fast sample rate from the relay made latency WORSE (~3s, fluctuating), not better.

Next steps: capture the app's exact ce060034 write on a direct connection; compare PM5->central notification rate direct vs through the relay; measure relay internal processing latency; try AcquireNotify/AcquireWrite FD pipes instead of PropertiesChanged.

Blocks feature-neutrality sign-off (Step C row 4). See docs/planning/log/pm5-ble-relay-hardware-validation-findings.md sections 11.1 / 11.1a. Related: c2m-bm7.5 (notification rate config char 0x0034).
notes: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED and fixed 2026-09-06 hardware run #2 on edge-04 (192.168.12.114), superseding the 'not established' verdict in the note above. The app writes 8 bytes (02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00, a little-endian 64-bit 2 = 250ms) to ce060034, which the spec and the real PM5 declare as 1 byte. The emulated server didn't enforce that length, so the full 8 bytes were forwarded as an ATT Write Request and the PM5 answered Invalid Attribute Value Length (0x0D) and discarded it -- the erg stayed at its 1Hz default the whole session while the app believed it had asked for 250ms. That is essentially the whole ~1s gap. Fix (12a4e62): truncate an over-length consumer write to the characteristic's declared length before forwarding -- reproduces the real erg's own ATT-layer contract. The relay's own forward path measures 1.2ms mean / 4.2ms max, so it was never the bottleneck. Prerequisite fix (ace886b): log the hex payload of an over-length write, not just its length -- needed to see the actual bytes. R-LATENCY-1's wording ('forward these writes intact, no rate policy') was revised: length clamping isn't a rate policy. Findings doc updated: docs/planning/log/pm5-ble-relay-hardware-validation-findings.md section 14.5. NOT YET HARDWARE END-TO-END VERIFIED: whether the PM5 actually speeds up and perceived app lag drops to something close to the 0.15s direct baseline is c2m-ooz.3.3's job.
close_reason: Root cause found and fixed (12a4e62, ace886b); end-to-end re-verification against the real PM5+app rolled into c2m-ooz.3.3

title: Implement PM5 BLE relay: Pi central + peripheral emulation (2 adapters)
description:
Build a working relay so the Pi can hold the sole BLE connection to the PM5 while a second BLE adapter emulates a PM5-like peripheral for the iPhone Concept2 app to connect to instead -- letting both MQTT publishing and the official app work at the same time.

Follows from c2m-ooz.1/c2m-ooz.2 (ADR-003): the PM5 only accepts one BLE connection, so the app and concept2mqtt can't both connect to the real PM5 directly. This feature is the considered-and-deferred Option 3 from ADR-003, now de-risked by hardware validation on 2026-08-08 (see ADR-003 amendment).
design:
Architecture: onboard adapter (hci0) stays dedicated to the real PM5 central connection (proven reliable throughout all prior testing). A second USB BLE adapter (hci1, confirmed working: CSR8510-class dongle) runs a GATT peripheral server emulating the PM5, registered via BlueZ's standard D-Bus LEAdvertisingManager1/GattManager1 APIs (e.g. via the bluez-peripheral Python library) -- NOT the raw btmgmt/MGMT-socket path, which was confirmed to produce a non-connectable device.

Requires a kernel build past the raspberrypi/linux#7473 regression (kernel 6.18.x broke LEAdvertisingManager1 registration system-wide with 'Invalid Parameters (0x0d)', independent of adapter; fixed via rpi-update to 6.18.42-v8+ or later).

Working hypothesis (unconfirmed): the official Concept2 iPhone app queries the proprietary CSAFE-over-BLE service (ce06xxxx UUID family) rather than the standard Fitness Machine Service (0x1826) the PM5 also exposes. Emulate the proprietary service first. If the app fails to recognize the relay, a BLE traffic capture of a real app session (e.g. via Xcode PacketLogger) would be needed to confirm what it actually queries.

Relay behavior: notifications from the real PM5 (central side) must be forwarded to the emulated peripheral's notify characteristics for the iPhone; writes from the iPhone to the emulated peripheral's command characteristics must be forwarded to the real PM5. A raw byte-level pass-through is sufficient for the relay itself -- no CSAFE decoding needed there (decoding for MQTT publishing is a separate, already-planned concern that can tap the same central-side notification stream).

Deferred: whether the onboard adapter alone (hci0) can reliably sustain central+peripheral simultaneously on one radio was deliberately not tested -- revisit once the two-adapter approach is stable in case it can simplify the hardware requirement.
acceptance_criteria:
- GATT server on the second adapter successfully emulates PM5 identity (name, Device Info characteristics) well enough for the official Concept2 iPhone app to connect to it as if it were the real PM5
- Live rowing data relayed from the real PM5 through the Pi to the iPhone app with acceptable latency (no perceptible lag during a workout)
- Commands/writes from the iPhone app are relayed through to the real PM5 and take effect
- concept2mqtt's MQTT publishing continues working unaffected via the same central-side PM5 connection
- Real PM5 connection on hci0 remains stable for an extended session (not just a few minutes) with the relay active
- A Pi-side capture of a real iPhone-app-to-relay session confirms which GATT service the official app actually queries -- the proprietary CSAFE-over-BLE family (ce06xxxx) or the standard Fitness Machine Service (0x1826). The Pi is the GATT server the app connects to, so the relay's --debug access log plus a btmon -i hci1 capture are sufficient; no Mac, Xcode PacketLogger or external sniffer is required. This open hypothesis must be resolved while building the emulated GATT server: building against the wrong service means the app will not recognize the relay as a PM5 at all.
- The emulated GATT server implements the confirmed service's full characteristic set -- not just identity, data and command characteristics -- closely enough that the iPhone app's core live-session functionality behaves the same through the relay as with a direct PM5 connection: connecting, live workout metrics display, start/stop/pause, and any other screens or interactions available during an active live session. Feature neutrality with a direct connection is the bar, not "connects and streams". Verification is a subjective pass/fail user acceptance check against a direct-connection baseline -- protocol-level logs are not required to sign it off.
- Any app feature found NOT to work identically through the relay during this validation is explicitly documented as a known gap (not silently dropped), with a note on whether it is deferred to c2m-hlj (Fast-Follow Features) or c2m-2rf (Extended Features).

notes: Hardware validation 2026-09-05: char 0x0034 (ce060034) is the crux of the relay latency defect c2m-ooz.3.1. Direct iPhone<->PM5 connection: app writes ce060034 (8-byte payload, twice, right after identity reads) and gets ~0.15s telemetry lag. Through the relay: the same write is forwarded but the PM5 keeps streaming General Status at ~1Hz -> ~1s lag. So the notification-rate configuration must (a) be forwarded to the PM5 in exactly the form it expects, and (b) actually be verified to take effect (read back the achieved notification rate, not just the ACK). The 8-byte write to a nominally 1-byte characteristic is unexplained - decode against docs/planning/spec/csafe. Also: naively forcing a fast rate from the relay made end-to-end latency WORSE. See docs/planning/log/pm5-ble-relay-hardware-validation-findings.md 11.1/11.1a.

title: Reconcile pm5_proprietary_profile advertised UUID (ce060000) with test_profile.py
description:
Hardware validation 2026-09-05 changed pm5_proprietary_profile to advertise pm5_uuid(0x0000) (ce060000-...) because the iPhone app scan-filters on that 128-bit UUID and would not otherwise list the relay. But test_profile.py still asserts advertised_service_uuids == (sig_uuid(0x1826),) (from an earlier lost session) - the unit test now FAILS against the working tree.

Reconcile:
- Decide the final advertised set. Real PM5 (BLE-5 extended adv) broadcasts: name + 16-bit 0x1826 + 128-bit ce060000 + Service Data 0x1826=01 10 00 + Appearance + TX power. A legacy adapter cannot fit all of it (BlueZ 'Failed to register advertisement').
- Open question: ce060000 is advertised but NOT in the served GATT tree (relay serves ce060010/20/30/40 + 1826). The real PM5's GATT tree also appears to start at ce060010 - confirm whether ce060000 needs a served service or is discovery-marker-only.
- Update test_profile.py to match; keep the _ServiceDataAdvertisement a{sv} subclass (real bluez-peripheral bug) even though service-data advertising is currently disabled.

Working-tree changes are also on the Pi at ~/concept2mqtt. See docs/planning/log/pm5-ble-relay-hardware-validation-findings.md sections 3.4, 4, 5, 9.
notes:
Done by commit 6016416 (2026-09-06).

- Final advertised set decided: (pm5_uuid(0x0000),) i.e. the 128-bit ce060000, no service data. Rationale: the app scan-filters on ce060000; 0x1826 alone and 0x1826+ServiceData both left the relay invisible; a legacy adapter cannot fit ce060000 + ServiceData + full name in 31 bytes.
- test_profile.py reconciled: now asserts (pm5_uuid(0x0000),) plus a new test that advertised_service_data is empty by default. The stale docstrings that still described the abandoned FTMS/ServiceData theory are rewritten.
